tool.name: FAIRe2ENA: experiments and runs
tool.description: convert FAIRe run metadata to ENA EXPERIMENT and RUN XML
tool.command: set -o pipefail; @LINK_INPUT@ python '$__tool_directory__/faire2ena_galaxy.py' run --input_file input.xlsx --receipt_file '$receipt_file' --study_accession '$study_accession' --center_name '$center_name' --instrument_model '$instrument_model' #if str($assay.assay_select) == 'one': --assay_name '$assay.assay_name' $assay.add_assay_suffix #end if #if str($seq_runs).strip(): --seq_run_id '$seq_runs' #end if #if str($ftp_subdir).strip(): --ftp_subdir '$ftp_subdir' #end if --experiment_output '$experiments_xml' --run_output '$runs_xml' --submission_file '$submission_xml' | tee '$log'

param.name: receipt_file
param.label: ENA sample receipt
param.help: The receipt XML that ENA returned when you submitted the samples. It links each samp_name to its ENA sample accession.

param.name: study_accession
param.label: ENA study accession
param.help: The accession of the ENA study (project) the runs belong to, for example PRJEB12345.

validator.message: Enter an ENA study accession such as PRJEB12345 or ERP123456

param.name: instrument_model
param.label: Sequencing instrument
param.help: Values from the ENA controlled list for the Illumina platform.

param.name: assay_select
param.label: Assays to include
param.help: A library that holds several assays (the same sample and files on each row) gets one experiment and run. If a library ID (lib_id) is used for more than one assay with different files, give each row its own lib_id, or submit each assay separately.

param.name: assay_name
param.label: assay_name
param.help: As written in the assay_name column of experimentRunMetadata, for example MiFish or ssu16sv4v5-emp.

param.name: add_assay_suffix
param.label: Add the assay name to experiment and run aliases
param.help: Keeps aliases unique when the same lib_id was sequenced for several assays.

param.name: seq_runs
param.label: Sequencing runs to include (optional)
param.help: seq_run_id values from experimentRunMetadata, comma-separated, for example RUN01,RUN02. Leave empty for all runs. Use it when the same lib_id was sequenced in more than one run: each run then goes in its own submission, as ENA needs a unique alias per library.

validator.message: Enter seq_run_id values separated by commas

param.name: ftp_subdir
param.label: FTP sub-directory of the read files
param.help: If you uploaded the fastq files into a folder in your Webin upload area, give its name here. It is added in front of each file name. Leave empty if the files are at the top level.

has_text.text: joined the rows of 4 libraries that hold several assays (ssu16sv4v5-emp and ssu18sv9-emp)
4 lib_ids name several assays (e.g. GOMECC16S_Neg1); FAIRe takes a library to be one amplicon of a sample
the experiment and run aliases are each library's own name: the lib_id without its assay_name and seq_run_id (e.g. GOMECC16S_Neg1_ssu16sv4v5-emp_20220613_Amplicon_PE250 -> GOMECC16S_Neg1)
no runs with seq_run_id 'RUN99'. Sequencing runs in the workbook: 20220613_Amplicon_PE250, 20220718_18S-Amplicon_PE250, 20220831_16S-Amplicon_PE250
Assays in the workbook: ssu16sv4v5-emp, ssu18sv9-emp

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool converts the **experimentRunMetadata** sheet of a FAIRe workbook into ENA EXPERIMENT and RUN XML files. It is the second of two steps: first run **FAIRe2ENA: samples**, submit the samples to ENA, and upload the receipt that ENA returns.
The tool converts only the rows whose samp_name appears in the receipt, so that each run is linked to its ENA sample accession. Other rows, for example controls you did not register, are skipped and listed in the log.
-----
**Inputs**
- **The same FAIRe workbook** you used for the samples. experimentRunMetadata needs samp_name, assay_name, lib_id, filename, filename2, checksum_filename and checksum_filename2 (the MD5 of each fastq.gz file). - **The ENA sample receipt** (XML). - **The ENA study accession** (PRJEB... or ERP...). - **Your centre name and the sequencing instrument.** - **Optionally**, one assay to include, the sequencing runs to include (seq_run_id), and the FTP folder that holds the read files.
**Outputs**
- **EXPERIMENT XML**: one experiment for each sequencing library, with the library's own name as its alias (plus the assay name, if you choose). - **RUN XML**: the forward and reverse fastq files and their MD5 checksums. - **SUBMISSION XML** (action ADD) and a **log**.
FAIRe defines a library as "an amplicon of a sample with unique MIDs". This means a library that holds several assays, such as amplicons pooled before indexing, has a row for each assay with the same sample and files, and the tool gives it one experiment and one run. The FAIRe mapper writes lib_id as the library name, assay_name and seq_run_id (M097_16SFish_LerayCOI_Fish16S_AGRF_2024-12), and the tool takes the assay and run off again for the aliases (M097_16SFish_LerayCOI). Where names would then repeat, it keeps the run, or failing that the whole lib_id.
-----
**Checks before conversion**
The tool stops, with a list of the problems, if any included row has an empty file name, a missing or malformed MD5 checksum, or a lib_id that is not unique, because ENA would reject these.
**Limitations**
- The tool writes only paired-end Illumina amplicon libraries (LIBRARY_STRATEGY AMPLICON, LIBRARY_SOURCE METAGENOMIC, LIBRARY_SELECTION PCR). - It does not upload the read files themselves. Upload them to your Webin upload area first, using ENA's FTP or Aspera instructions, then submit these XML files with the Webin REST service, for example::
curl --proto-default https -u Webin-XXXXX:PASSWORD -F "SUBMISSION=@submission.xml" \ -F "EXPERIMENT=@experiments.xml" -F "RUN=@runs.xml" \ wwwdev.ebi.ac.uk/ena/submit/drop-box/submit/
This address is ENA's test server. For the real submission, use www.ebi.ac.uk in place of wwwdev.ebi.ac.uk.
